chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, said,
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The basil is of twenty one types, the chief of it is the myrtle.
ai.seo_question: What are the different types of basil according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies twenty-one varieties of basil (rayhan), designating the myrtle (as) as the chief among them, reflecting the Shia tradition of detailed natural classification (tabaqat). This narration highlights the spiritual and physical virtues attributed to specific plants in Islamic tradition, where 'rayhan' often symbolizes divine pleasure and fragrant goodness. The emphasis on myrtle underscores its status not merely as a botanical entity but as a symbol of purity and blessedness in both material and metaphysical realms.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, raising it, said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The basil is of twenty one types, the chief of it is the myrtle’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from in a marfu‘ manner the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Sweet basil is of twenty-one kinds and the master among them is myrtle.’”
